transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-04-12
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Sarah Kim (Redwood AE), Raj Patel (Redwood SE), Emily Chen (Phoenix Payments - Eng Mgr), Carlos Ortiz (Phoenix - Platform Eng), Lena Park (Phoenix - Security)

[00:00] Sarah: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check — audio ok? ... cool. I'm Sarah, I'm the AE, and Raj our SE will run through the SDKs and quickstarts. Emily, you said this is mostly an integration walkthrough and auth questions? 

[00:18] Emily: Yep, that's right. We're evaluating Redwood for a payments assistant use case — transaction insights, AML flagging, and internal summarization. Primary concerns are auth (SSO/KMS), on-prem vs hosted, and integration velocity with our Node services and Python data pipelines.

[00:35] Raj: Great. We'll do a live walk through for the Python and TypeScript SDKs, show streaming, env setup, and the console bits (Optimize recommendations and telemetry). We'll also touch on Dedicated vs Hosted for compliance.

[00:48] Sarah: Also quick note on timeline — you mentioned a pilot. What timeframe are you thinking? 

[00:55] Emily: Ideally a 2-4 week pilot to validate latency and cost. If things look good, we want to be into production by Q3.

[01:05] Sarah: Sounds doable, we'll map next steps. Alright Raj, over to you.

--- SDK Quickstart (TS/Python) ---
[01:15] Raj: Ok first slide — installing the SDK. For Node/TypeScript it's npm i @redwood-inference/sdk (note: some transcriber shows 'red wood' but it's redwood-inference). Example snippet:

[01:28] Raj: "const Redwood = require('@redwood-inference/sdk'); const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY }); const res = await client.generate({ model: 'rw-medium-1', prompt: 'Summarize...'});"

[01:45] Carlos: Quick question — we prefer SSO via SAML and API keys for services. How does that map? 

[01:52] Raj: Good q. For human users we integrate SSO/SCIM via SAML or OIDC — that's for Console access. For services you provision long-lived API keys scoped to routes and optionally tie to RBAC. You can also enable short-lived tokens with your IDP via the Private control plane integration. (mumbles: support for k-m-s) — we support KMS/HSM integrations for key wrapping, and customer-managed keys for Private.

[02:20] Lena: Can you send the SOC2 and KMS docs after? We have an audit next month.

[02:25] Sarah: Absolutely, we'll share SOC2, ISO artefacts and our security whitepaper. Raj I'll ping you to attach the KMS integration notes.

--- Env Setup ---
[02:35] Raj: For local envs, set REDWOOD_API_KEY in your .env. In typescript app, example flow: import client, set model + streaming handler. For streaming we show both SSE and Websocket. Snippet:

[02:50] Raj: "client.stream({model:'rw-large-2', prompt:'...'}, (chunk)=>{ process.stdout.write(chunk.text) })" — note that streaming lowers client perceived latency and works over our hosted or dedicated endpoints.

[03:10] Emily: How is streaming billed — per token? Any extra overhead?

[03:15] Raj: It's per-token same as normal generation. There is minimal connection overhead but no separate charge. Also you can adjust batch/window settings from the Console Optimize tab to reduce cost.

[03:28] Carlos: On Dedicated vs Hosted — we need data isolation and SLA. What's the recommended approach for us?

[03:34] Raj: For payments and regulated PII, Dedicated or Private (VPC) is common. Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput. Private gives you a customer-managed control plane and KMS integration. Hosted is fastest to start. For a pilot we often do hosted with VPC peering + strict retention, then move to Dedicated if throughput and isolation needs increase.

[03:58] Emily: Ok that matches our thinking.

--- Quickstarts and Examples ---
[04:05] Raj: I pulled up the quickstart repo — github.com/redwood-inference/quickstarts (note: link may be slightly mangled in transcription). Inside there's python/ts folders. Python example uses pip install redwood-sdk, then:

[04:20] Raj: "from redwood_sdk import RedwoodClient; client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY']); resp = client.chat.create(model='rw-chat-1', messages=[{'role':'user','content':'Summarize TX 12345'}])"

[04:37] Emily: Any differences in behavior between SDKs? We run async workers in Python (Celery) and Node event loop.

[04:44] Raj: SDKs are parity for core features. Python supports sync/async, TypeScript naturally async. Both include streaming, embeddings, and function calling. For heavy throughput we recommend the TypeScript/Node SDK for frontend edge cases due to event-loop friendliness but Python is fine for batch pipelines.

[05:05] Carlos: Do you have sample integration for our Kafka-based pipeline?

[05:10] Raj: Yes there's a connector example that shows consuming, batching requests to the Redwood endpoint, and using prefix caching. I'll upload that link after the call.

--- Auth / Network ---
[05:22] Raj: About auth and network, two patterns we see: 1) Server-to-server API keys with RBAC + per-route scopes; 2) Short lived tokens via your IDP and our token exchange for ephemeral access. For VPC/Private we support private endpoints and can deploy within customer VPC for egress control.

[05:40] Lena: For logging — does the platform store prompts? We need redact or disable storage.

[05:46] Raj: You can configure retention policies at the project level. For Dedicated/Private you can opt out of retention and disable prompt logging; also we support field-level redaction and post-call hooks to scrub PII. We'll share the docs. (transcriber: 'post call' sometimes read as 'post code')

--- Performance / Benchmarks ---
[06:10] Raj: For latency, sample numbers are on the model catalog. For small chat models you can expect p50 ~ 80-150ms per token in our hosted for rw-medium; larger models increase. For production we tune batching and KV cache; Optimize gives recommendations automatically based on traffic profiles.

[06:28] Carlos: Can we run our own benchmarks in the pilot? E.g., 99th percentile latency under load?

[06:33] Raj: Yes — we typically do a benchmark run against a dedicated pilot node or hosted infra; we can spin up a dedicated pool for short window. We'll need a dataset and target SLOs.

[06:45] Emily: Great. For cost predictions, does Console show token-level breakdowns per route?

[06:51] Raj: Yes Console has per-route, per-token cost breakdowns, and Optimize can suggest batching and quantization to lower spend.

--- Demo: Console Walkthrough ---
[07:02] Raj: (screen share) Console -> Projects -> SDK Quickstart. Shows API key creation and route scoping. Also the Optimize tab shows suggested batch size and cache TTL based on observed seq length distribution.

[07:25] Emily: One thing — we use GCP and want region control. Can you pin regions?

[07:30] Raj: Yes, you can route by region and pin model variants; Private supports on-prem as well. For Hosted we offer region selection for provisioning.

--- Questions and Objections ---
[07:45] Carlos: Competitors like OpenAI and Anthropic — any migration story?

[07:50] Sarah: You can bring your prompts and evals; our prompt layer tries to be model-agnostic, and we support common APIs. For model parity we have curated open models in the catalog and conversion layers for call signatures.

[08:05] Emily: Our security team will want to review the SOC2 docs and auditable logs.

[08:10] Sarah: We'll circulate those today, plus contact for the security PM. Lena: I'll put you directly in touch with our compliance lead.

--- Recap & Next Steps ---
[08:20] Sarah: To recap: Raj will share the quickstart repo, Python/TS snippets, Kafka connector, and SDK examples. I'll send pricing/pilot terms and security docs. Emily will confirm pilot dataset and timing.

[08:35] Emily: Yep, I'll put together a 1pager with dataset and target SLOs and Slack the group.

[08:42] Sarah: Great. Any last q's?

[08:45] Lena: No, just to confirm — KMS/HSM docs and SOC2.

[08:50] Sarah: Affirmative. We'll send. Thanks everyone.

[09:00] (call ends)

Notes on transcript quality: Some transcribed product names appear as 'red wood' or 'red wood inference' and 'vertex ai' lowercased. There were a few overlaps and filler words removed for brevity. Links referenced: github.com/redwood-inference/quickstarts (to be shared), security docs (will be attached).
